subject: English
chapter: Journey to the End of the Earth
central_question: How does an Antarctic journey reveal Earth’s geological history, the scale of human impact and the urgent interdependence of all life?
in_scope_units: Before you read and the journey aboard the Akademik Shokalskiy from Madras to Antarctica.
Part of history: Gondwana, continental separation, geological processes and Antarctica’s scale.
Human impact: population, fossil fuels, carbon dioxide, climate change and ice-core records.
Students on Ice and Geoff Green’s educational purpose.
Antarctica’s simple ecosystem, phytoplankton, ozone depletion, food chain and carbon cycle.
Walk on the ocean: the ice-pack experience near Tadpole Island and the revelation that everything connects.
Reading with Insight Questions 1–4 on geological history, students, small changes and past-present-future.
banned_topics: Climate data, scientific predictions or Antarctic facts not included in the chapter.
A full scientific account of plate tectonics or photosynthesis beyond the explanations in the text.
Current information from the Students on Ice website.

known_pitfalls.claim: Antarctica has always been cold and separate from India.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter says India and Antarctica were once part of Gondwana, when the climate was warmer.

known_pitfalls.claim: The chapter gives a certain prediction that the West Antarctic ice sheet will melt completely.
known_pitfalls.correction: It asks uncertain questions—‘Maybe. Maybe not’—while presenting climate change as a real threat.

known_pitfalls.claim: Phytoplankton are unimportant because they are microscopic.
known_pitfalls.correction: They nourish the Southern Ocean food chain and influence marine life and the global carbon cycle.

known_pitfalls.claim: Students on Ice is mainly a holiday for celebrities.
known_pitfalls.correction: Geoff Green shifted from wealthy curiosity-seekers to high school students who can learn and act as future policy-makers.

recommended_example_progression: Use Reading with Insight Q1 to connect geological records with human understanding.
Use Reading with Insight Q4 to integrate Antarctica’s past, present and future.
Use Reading with Insight Q2 to analyse Geoff Green’s choice of students.
Use Reading with Insight Q3 to interpret the phytoplankton metaphor.
Use the Walk on the ocean episode to conclude with interdependence and planetary balance.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Reading with Insight Questions 1–4 on geological history, Students on Ice, small environmental changes and Antarctica’s record of Earth’s past, present and future.
